info.title: Thicket
info.description: Thicket's versioned REST API. The web app runs on the same routes, so everything the product does is here. Human-readable reference: https://www.thickethq.com/developers/api

get.description: Identity, owners, plan limits, can-do flags, and settings for the caller's organization (any member). `logo` is omitted when unset.

patch.description: Owner only. A new name gives the account a new address: its slug is rebuilt as `{slugified-name}-{key}` around its permanent `key`, and the answer carries it. Every earlier address keeps resolving in the `{orgSlug}` segment (by the key, and a pre-July workspace's pre-rename slug by `legacy_slug`, which its first rename sets), and the API never redirects, so a path built from an old slug keeps working. A client holding the workspace by `id` or `key` sees no change; one holding it by slug refreshes its organization list.

name.description: Validated as POST /orgs validates a name: 1 to 100 characters with at least one letter or number in any script (422 invalid otherwise). Refused with 422 (invalid) when it carries a link: a scheme such as https://, a www. address, or a domain followed by a path. A bare domain such as Linear.app is a name and is accepted. Resending the current name is always accepted and changes nothing, even one set before these rules.

slug.description: The account's address now: rebuilt from the new name around the permanent key when the name changed it, the same slug otherwise.

409.description: The new name would give the account an address another account has (`conflict`). Choose a different name.

delete.description: Owner only, effective immediately: the org turns invisible everywhere, any Stripe subscription is cancelled, and every owner gets a confirmation email. Data is retained for a 30-day restore window (POST /api/v1/orgs/{orgId}/restore); after that the purge task hard-deletes rows and storage.

get.description: Owner only; the response is a JSON attachment. `?projects=id,id` limits content to those projects (people, companies, and groups always ride along). Private chats and personal notes are never included; use /account/export/chats for transcripts.

parameters.name: projects
parameters.description: Comma-separated project ids to limit the content

get.description: Owner only; deliberately split from the account export because of the privacy weight it carries. Transcripts (participants plus author, timestamp, and content lines) for the chosen conversations, as a JSON attachment.

parameters.name: ids
parameters.description: Comma-separated DM recording ids, at least one

put.summary: Upload or replace the account logo
put.description: Admin and up. Multipart upload, `logo` field, any decodable image up to 5 MB; the server re-encodes it to a square webp.

delete.description: Admin and up.

get.summary: Storage usage vs the plan limit
get.description: Total usage, the plan's limit, and the largest files. Private-chat and unposted-draft uploads count toward usage but are never listed.

Everything that happened across your accessible projects, newest first, ready to group by day client-side. Page with `per_page` and follow the `Link: rel="next"` header, whose URL carries the next page's opaque `cursor` (rows written between requests neither repeat nor shift pages); `page` still answers. Same visibility rules as the Latest-activity page: trashed content and non-client-visible recordings filtered, chat and DM lines never logged. Filters: `project_id`, `person_id` (the actor), `starred=1` (your starred projects), `since` (ISO datetime), `q` (matches title, actor name, or content text).

parameters.name: person_id
parameters.description: Only this actor's events

parameters.name: starred
parameters.description: Pass 1 to limit to your starred projects

parameters.name: since
parameters.description: Only events at or after this instant

parameters.name: action
parameters.description: Comma list of event actions, e.g. card_added,move (a container-watch poll)

parameters.name: recording_type
parameters.description: Only events about recordings of this type

parameters.name: parent_id
parameters.description: Only events about recordings inside this container (a column, a list): the container-watch poll

parameters.name: q
parameters.description: Keyword filter: title, actor name, content text, or the name of someone added to a project (an `access_changed` row)

200.description: Activity events, newest first (default page size 50)

get.description: People only, in the named-agents pilot (`403 agents_unavailable` elsewhere). Owners and admins see every agent; anyone else sees only their own personal agent. Project names are filtered to the caller's access. Who may give an agent work is the connector's local setting (`thicket connect setup`).

post.description: Owners and admins only (Admin › Manage agents). Creates a shared agent: a member with no sign-in that reaches only the projects it is given. A personal agent is created by its owner on the connection approval page.

patch.description: `{name, project_ids}` renames the agent and replaces its projects: owners and admins for a shared agent, its owner for a personal one (projects the caller can see; hidden ones are kept). `{enabled: false}` deletes the agent (its owner, or an owner or admin): its connection is revoked, running work is interrupted, and its past content keeps it as the author. `{enabled: true}` answers 422: a deleted agent can't be restored.

delete.description: Its owner (personal) or an owner or admin. An agent has one connection; its tokens stop working on their next request and its listening session ends. A request already in progress may finish.

post.summary: Attach a file to rich text
post.description: Stores a file for a post's rich text: embed the returned `url` in the post's HTML (an `img` src for an image, an `audio` src for a voice note, an `a` href otherwise). Creating or saving the post that embeds it makes it that post's attachment: an `upload` recording with this same id whose parent is the post, listed in the post's `content_attachments` and by `GET /recordings/{post_id}/children?type=upload`, never in Docs & Files. It takes the post's audience, is trashed and restored with it, and stays with it if a later edit drops the embed. Until a post claims it, only its uploader can read it (`url`, `download_url`), and a file no post claims is deleted after 24 hours. Two forms. `multipart/form-data` with `file` (required, up to 50 MB) stores the bytes at once and answers the stored file. `application/json` with `filename` and `byte_size` (up to 10 GB) reserves the file and answers presigned storage URLs (`mode` `single`: PUT the whole file to `url` with the same `content_type`; `multipart`: PUT each `part_size` slice to `part_urls[n-1]` and keep each response's ETag), so the bytes go straight to storage; then call `completeAttachment`. A reservation is not ready, readable or claimable until completed; cancel it with `abandonAttachment`. Send the composer's place: `project_id` for a post in a project, or `dm_id` for a line in a direct message (a participant's, clients included); with neither (My Notes), only members of the team may attach, and both is a 422. A dm line that embeds the file claims it like any post, so deleting the line deletes it. Returns 402 when the plan's storage cap is reached. Files for Docs & Files go to `POST /recordings/{folder_id}/uploads` instead; `POST /recordings/{dm_id}/uploads` still posts a file straight into a dm (its cover image).

file.description: The file bytes, up to 50 MB, non-empty

project_id.description: The project of the post the file will be attached to

dm_id.description: The direct message whose line the file will be attached to (instead of project_id)

byte_size.description: The file's exact size in bytes, up to 10 GB; complete checks the stored object against it

content_type.description: Sent again as the PUT's Content-Type in single mode

project_id.description: The project of the post the file will be attached to

dm_id.description: The direct message whose line the file will be attached to (instead of project_id)

201.description: The multipart form: the stored file, waiting for a post to claim it. The JSON form: the reservation and its presigned storage URLs

delete.description: Deletes a file from `POST /attachments` that no post has claimed yet, for a composer whose author removed it before posting, or cancels a reservation mid-transfer (its stored parts go too). Only the uploader's own; once a post has claimed the file it belongs to the post and this answers 404 (edit the post instead).

parameters.name: attachmentId
parameters.description: The id `POST /attachments` returned

post.description: After PUTting the bytes of a file reserved with `createAttachment`'s JSON form: completes the multipart upload (send every part's ETag in `parts`; a single PUT sends no body), checks the stored object is the size reserved, and makes the file ready, so the post that embeds its `url` claims it and its uploader can read it. Only the uploader's own; answering again for a ready file is harmless. A file whose stored size differs is scrapped (404): reserve it again.

parameters.name: attachmentId
parameters.description: The id `POST /attachments` returned

etag.description: The ETag header storage answered that part's PUT with

200.description: The verified file, waiting for a post to claim it

get.description: Tier, subscription status, trial and period dates, plus usage against the plan's limits. In `limits`, -1 means unlimited; one `people` pool covers members and guests alike, clients included.

post.summary: Switch plans on the live subscription
post.description: Owner only. Swaps the price on the existing Stripe subscription with prorations, never a second subscription, and syncs the local row in-request so the change reads back immediately. 404 when there is no live subscription; 422 when the account is already on that plan. A downgrade below the org's active-project count is allowed: the org lands over-limit and the home chooser archives projects down, restorably.

Owner only. Verifies the price (from GET /api/billing/prices) and returns a Checkout URL to redirect the buyer to. The signup trial is the only trial an org ever gets: a session created mid-trial carries a trial_end aligned to the existing end date, never restarted, and every other org is charged at checkout. Under 48 hours of trial left checks out as an immediate charge. An account that already holds a subscription is refused with 409 already_subscribed: plan changes go through POST /billing/change-plan, the card and invoices through POST /billing/create-portal.

400.description: Unknown, inactive, or non-Thicket price (code bad_request)

409.description: The account already has a subscription (code already_subscribed); change plans with POST /billing/change-plan

post.summary: Create a Stripe customer portal session
post.description: Owner only: payment method, invoices, and cancellation. The optional `{"flow": "subscription_cancel"}` body deep-links the portal's cancel-subscription confirmation (404 without a subscription). Plan switching is not portal work; it rides /billing/change-plan.

get.description: Published platform announcements, newest first: global content read through an org-scoped URL, personalized per viewer ({{first_name}} interpolated, excerpts capped at 200 chars).

The way to open an `action: "announced"` notification row (those carry a bulletin_id instead of a recording_id). Published bulletins read for anyone in the org; a draft reads only for someone holding their own tray row for it (a test send), everyone else gets 404. Reading marks the caller's notification row read, same as opening the page.

200.description: The announcement, personalized for the caller

get.description: Events (and optionally due tasks) across every accessible project's calendar plus the account calendar. Recurring events expand at read time: each occurrence arrives as its own row carrying `occurrence_key`, the anchor-zone day key the occurrences DELETE endpoint speaks. `from`/`to` accept ISO 8601 with an explicit offset, or a zoneless wall clock interpreted in the caller's resolved zone (their /me timezone preference, then the tz cookie, then UTC).

parameters.name: from
parameters.description: Window start; offset or zoneless wall clock

parameters.name: to
parameters.description: Window end

parameters.name: just
parameters.description: `me`: only items you created or are invited to

parameters.name: tasks
parameters.description: Include due to-dos and cards (per-request view state, not persisted)

parameters.name: projects
parameters.description: Comma-separated project ids to limit to

parameters.name: calendars
parameters.description: Comma-separated calendar container ids (a project `calendar` tool's `container_id`, up to 50) to limit events to, so a project's extra Calendar shows only its own events. Pair it with `projects` for one project's calendar page. Dated to-dos and cards (`tasks`) are the project's and are not narrowed by it.

parameters.name: starred
parameters.description: Limit to your starred projects

post.description: Invitees (`participant_ids`) are notified. `project_id` null or omitted targets the account calendar: org-level events with no project, non-clients only. Datetimes accept an explicit offset or a zoneless wall clock resolved in the caller's zone. All-day events are floating dates, encoded T00:00:00Z to T23:59:59Z by convention.

project_id.description: null or omitted: the account calendar

calendar_id.description: Which of the project's calendars (a `calendar` tool's `container_id`) when it holds several; omitted: its first. Ignored for the account calendar; another project's calendar is 404

content_html.description: Rich notes (sanitized); wins over `content` when both are sent

link.description: A join link (video call etc.); reminders carry it

recurrence.description: The repeat schedule; null means the event does not recur (clears it on update)

participant_ids.description: Membership ids to invite; they are notified

visible_to_clients.description: A project event's "Who should see this?"; omitted means the project's `share_new_items_with_clients` default. Ignored on the account calendar

patch.description: Edits apply to the whole series for recurring events; to change one day, or one day onward, use the occurrences PATCH endpoint, and to delete them the occurrences DELETE. Invitees are notified of the change. Same fields as create, all optional. `recurrence: null` stops the event recurring. A series keeps its own `exdates` whatever the request sends: each names a day that lives on as its own event or in the trash.

content_html.description: Rich notes (sanitized); wins over `content` when both are sent

recurrence.description: The repeat schedule; null means the event does not recur (clears it on update)

get.description: "Add to my calendar": the event as a credential-authenticated iCalendar download (Content-Disposition: attachment). Recurring events export a year of occurrences. For an ongoing subscription mint a feed instead.

delete.summary: Delete an occurrence of a recurring event
delete.description: The trash prompt for recurring events ("Only delete this event" / "Also delete all future events"); recurring events only. What's deleted goes to the trash (`trashed_id`), and restoring it (`PUT /recordings/{trashed_id}/status/active`) puts the dates back into the series. Default: just this occurrence (`result: excluded`; the day is trashed as its own event). `?mode=future`: this and every later occurrence (`result: truncated`; the series ends the day before and the rest is trashed as one repeating event); from the first occurrence that trashes the whole series (`result: trashed`, `trashed_id` is the event itself). `date` is the occurrence's `occurrence_key`, the anchor-zone day key from the calendar listing; never derive it from `start` client-side. 404 when the series has no occurrence that day.

parameters.name: date
parameters.description: The occurrence's anchor-zone day key (YYYY-MM-DD)

parameters.name: mode
parameters.description: `future`: also delete all later occurrences

trashed_id.description: What went to the trash; restoring it undoes the deletion

patch.summary: Edit an occurrence of a recurring event
patch.description: The edit prompt for recurring events. Default ("No, just change this event"): the day splits off as its own event, linked to the series by `series_id` and `occurrence_key`, and takes the edit. `?mode=future` ("Yes, change future occurrences too"): the series ends the day before and a copy repeating from this day takes the edit; from the first occurrence the whole series is edited in place. Invitees hear about the change as with any edit, and a new date or time logs `rescheduled`. Returns the event that now carries the change, or the series unchanged when nothing changed. Same fields as editing an event, all optional. 404 when the series has no occurrence that day.

parameters.name: date
parameters.description: The occurrence's anchor-zone day key (YYYY-MM-DD)

parameters.name: mode
parameters.description: `future`: this and every later occurrence

content_html.description: Rich notes (sanitized); wins over `content` when both are sent

recurrence.description: `?mode=future` only: how the event repeats from this day on (a single day repeats with its series). `exdates` is ignored

get.description: Your active (unrevoked) feeds. Each `url` is a capability URL: the token in the path is the only credential the public /feeds/{token}.ics endpoint checks, so treat it like a password. Revoked feeds return 404 there.

post.description: A token-authenticated read-only ICS feed honoring the filters, for subscribing an external calendar app. The returned `url` is the capability: anyone holding it can read the feed until you revoke it. Clients cannot mint feeds and receive 404.

project_id.description: Legacy single-project scope; cannot be combined with project_ids

project_ids.description: Selected projects and/or the account calendar. Omit for all calendars. Cannot be combined with project_id.

starred_only.description: Follow your starred projects as they change (the calendar's Starred pick). Cannot be combined with project_id or project_ids (422).

url.description: The public /feeds/{token}.ics URL; the token is the credential

project_ids.description: Acknowledged selection, or null for all calendars

delete.description: Effective immediately: the feed's public URL starts returning 404. Only your own feeds are revocable.

get.description: Prefill for the event form: "Team call Friday at 10am" becomes a title plus a start (and end, when a range was given). A suggestion the user confirms, never a silent commit. Relative dates and clock times mean the viewer's zone. When nothing date-like is found, the datetime fields come back null.

parameters.name: q
parameters.description: The text to parse

get.description: Defaults are seeded per organization.

post.description: Admin and up.

patch.description: Admin and up.

delete.description: Admin and up; deleting clears the category from posts.

get.description: Your conversations, latest activity first, with participants and a preview of the last line. Direct chats have no project, never appear in activity, and are visible only to their participants. `?status=archived` lists archived ones: readable (and searchable) forever, but no new lines post into them.

post.description: Finds the existing conversation with exactly these people or starts one; either way the `dm` recording comes back with 201. Your own id alone starts a chat with just yourself. You can message admins, owners, and anyone you share a project with. Lines are chat children: POST /recordings/{chat_id}/children with type chat_message; archive via PUT /recordings/{id}/status/archived (for everyone, cannot be undone).

delete.description: Only whoever left the cheer, or an org admin or owner (403 otherwise; 404 when already gone). Works for recording cheers and event cheers alike.

get.description: Companies with counts of active memberships, the account's primary company first (`is_primary`), then by name. Removed memberships are excluded.

patch.description: Rename, toggle client status, or toggle `dms_disabled` (the per-company private-chat restriction: members drop from chat pickers, can't start DMs, and existing conversations freeze read-only both ways). The account's primary company is renamed here, apart from the account's own name, and can't be made a client company (403 `primary_company`).

delete.description: People keep their membership; they just lose the company association. The account's primary company can't be deleted (403 `primary_company`).

post.summary: Turn a URL into sanctioned embed markup
post.description: Server-generated embed markup for the allowlist: YouTube, Vimeo, Loom, Spotify, X, Flickr, Imgur, SoundCloud, and direct `.gif` URLs. Non-allowlisted URLs return `{html: null}`: keep a plain link. Client-supplied iframe HTML is never accepted anywhere; the returned markup also round-trips the rich-text sanitizer.

200.description: The markup, or null for a non-allowlisted URL

get.description: Every event across the projects you can see, oldest first in strict (created_at, id) order, so a poller that keeps the `position` each page answers never misses a row and never sees one twice: pass it back as `cursor` to read on from there. `since` starts a fresh read at an instant; `project_id` narrows to one project (and is how the sample project is read). Up to 100 a page; `has_more` says whether a page is full. Rows carry `performed_by` (the actor's membership id), `actor_kind` and `authored_via` (the machine channel that wrote what the event is about, or null for a person's own work). Same visibility rules as the activity timelines: trashed content and what a client cannot see stay out, chat and direct-message lines are never logged.

parameters.name: per_page
parameters.description: Rows per page; default and at most 100

parameters.name: since
parameters.description: Start a fresh read at this instant

parameters.name: project_id
parameters.description: Only this project's events

200.description: A page of events, oldest first, and the position to resume from

position.description: Pass as `cursor` on the next read; the last row's position, or the one you passed when nothing new arrived, null on a first empty read

get.summary: List cheers on a change-log event
get.description: Cheers on one row of a recording's change log. The per-recording events listing already inlines the same shape.

post.description: Up to 16 characters of text or emoji. Pings the event's actor through their `notify_cheers` channel, bundled into one notification per recording within 3 hours. An exact duplicate returns 200 `{already_cheered: true}` instead of 201.

200.description: Already cheered with exactly this content

get.description: Account-wide home-screen groupings of projects. Move a project in or out via PATCH /projects/{id} with `folder_id` (or null).

post.description: Any non-client member can manage folders; clients get 403.

patch.summary: Rename, recolor, or reorder a folder
patch.description: Any non-client member; clients get 403.

delete.description: The folder's projects drop back to the top level. Any non-client member; clients get 403.

get.description: Groups bundle non-client people for @-mentions and pickers. Removed memberships are excluded; groups with no active members remain in the list.

200.description: The organization's groups with their members

get.description: Owners and admins only; anyone else gets 403. Each merge keeps the merged-away person's address.

post.description: Irreversible dedupe: the winner inherits the loser's assignments, subscriptions, project access, and authorship.

get.description: Agent identities only. Oldest first, up to 100 requests from the last 30 days. Everything addressed to the agent lands here, from any person or agent but itself, on content it can read: `mentioned`, `assigned`, `subscribed` (a new comment or chat line where it follows), `watched` (a new to-do or card in a list or column it watches), `pinged` (a direct message), `completed` (something it follows was completed) and `cheered` (a cheer on its own post). Who may direct the agent is decided by its connector from local settings. A pending request whose source changed or that the agent can no longer read is dismissed. Terminal or running rows whose content is no longer readable carry only id, status and result.

post.summary: Claim, settle or dismiss a request
post.description: Requires the live runtime lease. `claim` moves a pending request to running (several can run at once; a second claim of one request fails). `completed`/`failed` settle work this runtime holds. `dismissed` closes a pending request the connector doesn't admit, with a short `result` (for example `not_trusted`). Posting a reply is a separate content operation, written as the agent.

post.summary: Start, renew or stop the listening lease
post.description: Agent identities only. Renew within 60 seconds; one runtime per agent (`403 agent_busy`). A runtime that takes the lease dismisses pending requests made more than a minute before it (`result: "before_this_run"`): requests made while nothing is listening are not picked up later. Stopping or losing the lease marks running requests interrupted; nothing is retried.

get.description: Open to-dos, cards and card steps assigned to you across projects, grouped into `priorities` (your Up Next list, in your order; items carry `priority_id`) and `non_priorities`. Card steps are normalized under their parent card as `children`: the card is pulled in even when only a step is assigned, and a prioritized step surfaces its card. Top-level items carry `assigned_to_me`, false only for a pulled-in parent card, which is not your assignment and cannot go Up Next. Schedule events you are invited to are not assignments: they live on /my/events and /my/do-today.
Completed to-dos, cards and card steps, newest first; assignments on archived or trashed recordings are excluded.

get.summary: Your dated assignments by due window
get.description: Dated open to-dos, cards and card steps in one due window. `overdue` is the default. Weeks start on your `week_start` preference (default `sunday`): `due_later_this_week` runs from the day after tomorrow through the week's last day and `due_next_week` is the seven days after it, computed in your time zone. The windows never overlap: on the week's last day, tomorrow is `due_tomorrow` only and `due_next_week` starts the day after.

200.description: Dated open assignments in the window

400.description: Invalid scope: the message lists the valid options

get.description: Your curated priority list, in your order; every row carries `priority_id`.

post.summary: Add an assignment to Up Next
post.description: Adds one of your own open assignments (a to-do, card or card step) to the bottom of Up Next (idempotent). Anything else, a schedule event included, is a 404.

patch.description: Send exactly one of `move` or `position`. `move` swaps the item with its neighbor in that direction. `position` moves it to that 1-based place in your Up Next list as `listUpNext` returns it (a position past the end puts it last) and renumbers the list, which is how the web page's drag reorders it. Items not in your Up Next list are a 404; both fields, neither, or a position under 1 is a 422.

move.description: Swap with the neighbor above or below.

position.description: The 1-based place to move the item to.

delete.summary: Drop an item out of Up Next
delete.description: The item returns to `non_priorities` on the assignments list.

get.description: Personal saved links to recordings, newest first. Only bookmarks the caller can still open are listed: one in a project they left, or on an item no longer shared with them, reappears if access returns.

post.description: Idempotent; the recording must be one you can see.

delete.description: Idempotent: removing a bookmark that is not there still succeeds.

get.summary: Cheers you have received and given
get.description: `{received, given}`, each newest first. Cheer notifications are their own channel, gated solely by the `notify_cheers` preference and never by the notify scope. `since` restricts both lists to cheers created after that instant. Each row includes `cheerer_membership_id`. Cheers do not create named-agent requests.

parameters.name: since
parameters.description: Only cheers created after this instant

get.description: `{events, tasks}` for today, side by side: your events plus your due assignments. The "today" window is computed in your resolved time zone, and each item carries `kind` (`event` or `task`).
Drafts across the org. Only ever returns the caller's own: drafts are shareable by direct link to non-client project members, but they stay unlisted everywhere, and every draft write is author-only.
Your upcoming events across all projects, recurring occurrences expanded. All-day events use the floating `T00:00:00Z` convention.

200.description: Events in the next 7 days, in start order

get.description: The next timed event starting within about 20 minutes (the countdown banner); `{event: null}` when nothing is imminent. A client gets the shared events they're on, as they get those events' reminders. `href` is the web app path to the event, carrying `?occurrence=` for a recurring occurrence.

link.description: The event's join link, when set

href.description: Web app path to the event

get.summary: Getting-started guide catalog and notification preference
get.description: Evergreen guides this role may open (none for clients; the invitation guide for owners and admins). Fetch message content using the existing bulletin detail endpoint. Reading there acknowledges the guide; the catalog does not mark anything read.

state.description: Where the person's sequence stands. active: guides may still be delivered. opted_out: the person stopped them. ended: the seven-day window passed. not_enrolled: no sequence (a client-only account, or an account that predates the feature).

stopped.description: True whenever nothing more will be delivered (state is not active). Offer the stop control only when false.

patch.description: Stops the sequence for this person across workspaces and marks its current-workspace messages read. Work notifications and email preferences are unchanged. The guides remain readable. Idempotent, and accepted in any state.

get.description: A `text/event-stream` that says, with ids only, when a line in the chat named by `chat` was posted, edited or deleted (`event: chat`, `data: {chat, line, action}`; a cheer on a line counts as `updated`) and when a notification row landed for you (`event: notification`, `data: {id}`). Fetch what changed through the ordinary reads: `GET /recordings/{chat}/children?type=chat_message` after your newest line, `GET /my/notifications`. Opens with `event: ready` carrying the server's build id, `transport` (`listen`, or `unavailable` when the server cannot push, in which case keep polling) and the chat it reports; sends `: ping` every 15 seconds; `event: resync` means events may have been missed, so catch up; `event: reconnect` ends the stream after ten minutes or when the server restarts, so open it again; `event: refused` (`data: {code, message, retryable}`) means you may no longer listen. `chat` must be a chat room or private chat you can read; without it the stream carries notifications alone. At most 6 open streams per person.

parameters.name: chat
parameters.description: The chat room or private chat whose line events to receive

get.description: My Notes: one private rich-text scratchpad per person, created empty the first time it is read. Only its creator can ever read it.

patch.description: The autosave. Saving what is already stored is a no-op that leaves `updated_at` alone. Pass `base_updated_at` to refuse a stale write: a 409 carries the current pad under `error.note` and writes nothing.

409.description: The pad changed since `base_updated_at`; nothing was written

post.description: Swaps the pad with its restore point (`previous_version`), so restoring again undoes the restore. 404 when there is no earlier version yet.

get.description: `{unread_count, notifications}`, newest first. Event and due-date reminders sweep lazily on every read (the count-only arm included) with DB-level dedupe, so reminder rows land exactly once even under concurrent reads. Reminder rows are delivery receipts, and the tray (and `unread_count`) shows only the newest per entry: one per event occurrence (its day-before, hour-before and starting-soon) and one per dated to-do or card (its due tomorrow, due today, overdue by a day and overdue by a week, across due-date changes); cursor reads return every receipt. Rows carry `bulletin_id` for platform announcements (action `announced`, actor-less) and `bundle_count` for chat rows: lines folded into one entry while it stayed unread. Project-chat rows use action `chatted` for the push-worthy idle-edge delivery and `chat_activity` for the quiet bundled tray row, both pointing at the room recording; visiting the room marks them read. **Cursor reads:** pass `since` (the last row's `created_at`) and `after` (its id) to walk forward, oldest first; the response then carries `next_cursor` to pass next time. Rows carry the actor's membership id, role and kind. Bundled notifications are context, not executable requests. Named agents use `/my/agent/inbox` and `/my/agent/session`.

A Person, Project, Item or Notes value that starts with `=`, `+`, `-`, `@`, a tab or a carriage return gets a leading apostrophe, so spreadsheets read it as text, never as a formula. schema.description: UTF-8 with no BOM, LF line endings and RFC 4180 quoting. Header `Date,Person,Hours,Regular,Overtime,Project,Item,Notes,Created` (then `Status` while approvals are on), then one row per counted entry, newest day first, then newest logged. No totals row. Hours is the combined total; Regular and Overtime are its two portions, all as decimal strings ("2.0", "1.5", "0.12"); Item is "{Type}: {title}" (To-do, Message, Document, File, Card or Event), empty for time on the project itself; Created is ISO 8601 with the caller's UTC offset. A Person, Project, Item or Notes value that starts with `=`, `+`, `-`, `@`, a tab or a carriage return gets a leading apostrophe, so spreadsheets read it as text, never as a formula. While approvals are on, a last `Status` column says where each entry's week stands: Approved, Submitted, Changed, Rejected or Not submitted.

post.description: The item must be active and one that takes time (to-do, message, document, file, card or event) in a project with its Timesheet on; the project's timesheet id logs time on the project itself. Each day of a repeating event is its own timesheet: pass `occurrence`, and the entry's `parent` is the recording holding that day (the series, a part of it, or the day split off on its own) with `occurrence_date` set. Events on the account calendar take no time. Writes no activity and sends no notification.

date.description: The day the time was spent; future days are accepted

hours.description: Combined regular and overtime hours, like 1.5 or 1:30. Must be positive; at most 24 hours a person a day across entries.

person_id.description: Whose time (a membership id); defaults to the caller. Admins and owners may name anyone on the project's team; members only themselves (403 otherwise)

overtime_hours.description: Overtime portion of the combined hours, like 1.5 or 1:30. Must be between zero and hours. Defaults to zero on create; omitted on update, preserves existing overtime up to the new total.

occurrence.description: Required for a repeating event: the day (the occurrence key from `?occurrence=` links). A day since split off the series is still that day

Header `Date,Person,Hours,Regular,Overtime,Project,Item,Notes,Created` (then `Status` while approvals are on), then one row per counted entry, newest day first, then newest logged. No totals row. Hours is the combined total; Regular and Overtime are its two portions, all as decimal strings ("2.0", "1.5", "0.12"); Item is "{Type}: {title}" (To-do, Message, Document, File, Card or Event), empty for time on the project itself, and the absence type for absence (Project "Absence"); Created is ISO 8601 with the caller's UTC offset. post.description: Legacy CLI compatibility. CLI 0.4 and later use OAuth authorization_code with PKCE at /api/oauth/token, targeting the /api/v1 resource. The exchange half of `thicket auth login`. Anonymous by design: the code plus the PKCE `code_verifier` are the credential. Any exchange attempt burns the code (single use), and refusals are indistinguishable (unknown, expired, used, or mismatched verifier all answer 401 `invalid_grant`). The response's `token` field is the only time the minted personal access token exists in plaintext. Rate-limited per caller address; 429 carries Retry-After.

The token acts as its user: same organizations, project access, role, and row-level security as their sign-in. `read`-scope tokens may only GET/HEAD (writes → 403 `read_only_token`). Bearer requests must send a User-Agent naming the app and a contact (URL or email) or they receive 400 `user_agent_required`. The web app's own session cookie is also accepted on every route.

It is the same session a browser holds in its cookie and is treated exactly like one: full scope, no User-Agent requirement, no token rate limit. Told apart from a personal access token by the `thicket_pat_` prefix, which session tokens never carry.
